sources.title: SpecTLB, ISCA 2011
sources.coverage: Predicted PA permits speculative memory activity while the real page walk later validates; incorrect prediction rolls back. Section3.3 identifies irreversible I/O effects and proposes speculative tagging, with exact implementation out of scope.
sources.limit: Cannot claim speculate-before-translation/then-validate as new. These read sections do not establish the specific cross-DID existing-issuer prefix adoption protocol. A predicted access may also hit local cache/MSHR, so no assertion every prediction necessarily adds DRAM traffic.

sources.title: InvisiSpec, MICRO 2018
sources.coverage: A later unsafe load can reuse an earlier requested/brought speculative-buffer line without a second hierarchy access; received data is copied to its own SB. Validation/exposure enforce consistency; LLC-SB can avoid a second main-memory access and invalidates stale data.
sources.limit: Speculative shadow reuse with no second access is an exact known component. The inspected protocol is per-core program-order speculative loads; it does not itself specify different IOMMU DID original DMA grants, PA/attrs/ordering validation after sampling or original AXI source-tail and physical W/B completion.

sources.title: SafeSpec 2018 preprint (not claimed as inspection of final DAC 2019 version)
sources.coverage: Shadow data can be reused by speculative instructions, moved on commit and freed on squash. Capacity can cause dropping or blocking; shared shadow-state contention needs security treatment.
sources.limit: Buffer/commit/discard is not new. This project protocol makes no side-channel isolation guarantee merely because data is hidden before authorization. The final author PDF was not retrieved; use inspected preprint only.

sources.title: EP4295236A1, Performing speculative address translation in processor-based devices
sections: Primary patent description paragraphs0002-0007 and0022-0025 as returned by indexed primary text
claims1/2/14/15 as returned by indexed primary text
sources.coverage: An enqueue or memory-pointer-referencing instruction extracts virtual addresses from a work descriptor and initiates speculative MMU translation to reduce peripheral paging delay.
sources.limit: Direct open failed; the indexed primary patent description and claims were available and read. This is descriptor-time translation/pre-touch context, not evidence that the existing-issuer data capture/adoption contract is implemented. No legal opinion or exhaustive claims coverage.

sources.title: SDM, PACT 2023
sources.coverage: Access-before-permit overlaps cached-data access with permission verification. A failed speculative write is rolled back using old replay data; an illegitimate session is isolated. Evaluation assumes speculation always succeeds because user-level PIN cannot extract access control.
sources.limit: This directly covers data/permission overlap across shared-memory computing nodes, so the nearest comparison cannot be limited to same-core CPU speculation. The inspected description does not establish passive reuse of an independently authorized DMA issuer with zero recipient logical exposure until its own IOMMU grant, no recipient predicted physical read and exactly-once original AXI tail recovery. Wrong permission/mapping outcomes are a meaningful boundary to investigate, not proof that SDM is generally incorrect.

judgement.covered_components: PA speculation; later validation; shadow buffering; data reuse before commit; avoiding a second hierarchy access.
judgement.specific_remaining_question: Does a closest implementation already close independent cross-DID own READ authorization and source-snapshot ordering after data sampling, then exactly-once complete the original DMA request with bounded one-tail recovery?
judgement.not_proof: A few inspected sources do not prove first publication. Conversely a hand-built fixed-history control using all new proposed interfaces is not a published prior merely by naming it ordinary.
judgement.closest_permission_neighbor: SDM access-before-permit is closer to the permission problem than a generic SB alone. A proposal needs a different exposure/recovery contract and explicitly evaluated failed/mismapped permissions; saying only CPU-vs-IOMMU is insufficient.
